We're building RecallOps India for neatHack 2026 (ends Oct 12, submission 7:00-11:55 PM IST). Read hackathon.md first, then the memory note neathack-recallops-status if you have it. Everything is in this folder.

What it is: an agent that reads Indian CDSCO drug-quality (NSQ) alerts, reconciles them against a distributor's synthetic stock and invoice records, places digital holds, traces which customers got held batches, verifies its own actions, and reopens decisions when a second alert adds batches. Pharma only (not food). Fixtures are synthetic and must be labelled so. "Not listed" is never a safety clearance.

Already done and committed: Entire is enabled, the repo is github.com/ibnweb3/recallops-india (private for now), recallops/alerts.py parses the real March 2025 CDSCO PDF (70 entries, tests pass), neatlogs works (NEATLOGS_API_KEY in .env, Python 3.13 in .venv).

Model access: .env has the hackathon LiteLLM key under the name LiteLLM. Please rename it to LITELLM_API_KEY. Base URL https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1 (OpenAI-compatible). Models: nova-micro, nova-lite, nova-pro, nova-2-lite, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6. The budget is $20 total, so keep calls cheap: code does the matching and arithmetic, the model only handles ambiguous rows, aliases and drafts. Never print or commit keys.

Rules: keep a log in hackathon.md (never delete entries, record only tests that really ran). Commit small and often with clear messages, ending each with the Co-Authored-By line. Don't make the repo public, post anything, or sign up for anything without asking me.

Next steps in order: (1) read a newer CDSCO alert from cdscoonline.gov.in/CDSCO/viewPublicNSQDrug and check the parser still works, (2) fixture generator: stock, invoices and downstream sales built from real batches, with deliberate messy rows, (3) naive name-only baseline, (4) the agent loop traced with neatlogs under separate workflowNames recallops-baseline and recallops-agent.

"""Parse a CDSCO monthly "NSQ Alert" PDF into structured entries.

Source: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, "NSQ Alert For The Month of ...".
Each alert lists drug batches that failed a quality test (Not of Standard Quality).
A failure is specific to the tested batch; it says nothing about other batches.

Dates in the alerts are month/year only (MM/YYYY), so they are kept as "YYYY-MM".
Raw cell text is preserved next to every parsed field so nothing is lost.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import pdfplumber

HEADER_KEYS = ("s.no", "product", "batch")
MONTH_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d{1,2})\s*/\s*(\d{4})\s*$")


@dataclass
class AlertEntry:
    source_file: str
    source_sha256: str
    page: int
    sno: str
    product_name: str
    batch_no: str
    mfg_month: str | None  # "YYYY-MM" or None when the cell did not parse
    expiry_month: str | None
    manufacturer: str
    nsq_result: str
    lab: str
    raw: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    issues: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def clean(text: str | None) -> str:
    """Collapse the line breaks and runs of spaces that PDF cells carry."""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (text or "").replace(" ", " ")).strip()


FULL_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d{1,2})\s*/\s*(\d{1,2})\s*/\s*(\d{4})\s*$")


def parse_month(cell: str) -> str | None:
    """MM/YYYY -> "YYYY-MM". A stray DD/MM/YYYY (seen in the March 2025 alert) keeps its month."""
    m = MONTH_RE.match(cell)
    if m:
        month, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    else:
        m = FULL_DATE_RE.match(cell)
        if not m:
            return None
        month, year = int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
    if not 1 <= month <= 12:
        return None
    return f"{year:04d}-{month:02d}"


def sha256_of(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def is_header(row: list[str | None]) -> bool:
    joined = " ".join(clean(c).lower() for c in row)
    return all(k in joined for k in HEADER_KEYS)


def parse_alert_pdf(path: str | Path) -> list[AlertEntry]:
    path = Path(path)
    digest = sha256_of(path)
    entries: list[AlertEntry] = []
    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
        for page_no, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
            for table in page.extract_tables():
                for row in table:
                    if not row or is_header(row):
                        continue
                    cells = [clean(c) for c in row]
                    if len(cells) < 8 or not (cells[1] or cells[5] or cells[6]):
                        continue  # blank or malformed row
                    sno, product, batch, mfg, exp, maker, result, lab = cells[:8]
                    if not sno and not batch and entries:
                        # An entry that straddles a page break leaves a fragment at the top of
                        # the next page: no S.No and no batch. It continues the previous entry,
                        # cell by cell, so join the text back on.
                        prev = entries[-1]
                        prev.product_name = clean(f"{prev.product_name} {product}")
                        prev.manufacturer = clean(f"{prev.manufacturer} {maker}")
                        prev.nsq_result = clean(f"{prev.nsq_result} {result}")
                        prev.lab = clean(f"{prev.lab} {lab}")
                        prev.issues.append(f"joined a continuation fragment from page {page_no}")
                        continue
                    issues = []
                    mfg_m, exp_m = parse_month(mfg), parse_month(exp)
                    if mfg_m is None:
                        issues.append(f"manufacturing date not MM/YYYY: {mfg!r}")
                    if exp_m is None:
                        issues.append(f"expiry date not MM/YYYY: {exp!r}")
                    if not batch:
                        issues.append("batch number is empty")
                    entries.append(
                        AlertEntry(
                            source_file=path.name,
                            source_sha256=digest,
                            page=page_no,
                            sno=sno.rstrip("."),
                            product_name=product,
                            batch_no=batch,
                            mfg_month=mfg_m,
                            expiry_month=exp_m,
                            manufacturer=maker,
                            nsq_result=result,
                            lab=lab,
                            raw={"mfg": mfg, "expiry": exp},
                            issues=issues,
                        )
                    )
    return entries


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 2:
        print("usage: python -m recallops.alerts <alert.pdf> [out.json]")
        return 2
    src = Path(argv[1])
    entries = parse_alert_pdf(src)
    out = Path(argv[2]) if len(argv) > 2 else Path("data/alerts/parsed") / (src.stem + ".json")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps([asdict(e) for e in entries], indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    bad = [e for e in entries if e.issues]
    print(f"{src.name}: {len(entries)} entries, {len(bad)} with parse issues -> {out}")
    for e in bad[:10]:
        print(f"  #{e.sno} {e.product_name[:40]!r}: {'; '.join(e.issues)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

# RecallOps India: proposed scope and constraints

Updated 10 October 2026. The user selected RecallOps and an India-focused solution. The packaged-food distributor segment below is a recommendation, not yet a validated customer or implemented product.

## Recommended starting customer and task

Start with an Indian packaged-food distributor that maintains batch-wise stock and dispatch records. The distributor serves identifiable retailers, so downstream tracing can use invoices rather than assume every consumer can be identified.

Proposed goal: given an authenticated Indian recall notice, reconcile affected batches across two warehouses and retailer shipments, apply authorized digital holds, verify the resulting inventory, and prepare a source-backed recall progress packet. Missing evidence and outstanding units remain explicit.

This makes India relevance concrete through local notices, batch records, supplier/retailer invoices, pack/carton conversions, and an appropriate regional language. It does not depend on assumptions about judges' preferences.

## Evidence supporting the India scope

- FSSAI implemented Food Recall functionality in FoSCoS on 18 March 2026. Stakeholders can view recall information; regulators and food businesses create records and subsequent actions through their logins. A public integration API and complete, timely data coverage have not been verified. [Implementation order and manual](https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2026/03/69bbb3b762053Order%20dt.%2018.03.2026_Implementation%20of%20Food%20Recall%20functionality%20in%20FoSCoS.pdf), [public recall view](https://foscos.fssai.gov.in/food-recall)
- FSSAI's recall rules describe distribution records containing suppliers/customers, purchase/delivery dates, lots/batches, pack size and manufacture/expiry dates. The presence and quality of these fields in a prospective customer's records still need checking. Regulatory termination and physical completion cannot be inferred from a database hold. [Food Recall Procedure Regulations](https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Food_Recall_Regulations.pdf)
- A real historical example is Patanjali Foods' 23 January 2025 disclosure reporting FSSAI's direction to recall packed red chilli powder batch AJD2400012. It supports a dated replay using genuine scope evidence; it does not establish the product's current recall status or implicate other batches. [Manufacturer disclosure](https://www.patanjalifoods.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Letter-to-SE-23.01.2025.pdf)
- TallyPrime supports batch records, manufacture/expiry dates and batch movement reports. These capabilities are a possible data foundation, not proof that a particular distributor uses them correctly or that a hold integration already works. [TallyPrime documentation](https://help.tallysolutions.com/tally-prime/inventory/manage-inventory-batch-wise-tally/)
- Existing competition includes GS1 India's DataKart Trace, which advertises ERP integration and targeted recalls. Our proposed advantage is investigating inconsistent records, recovering from failed actions and verifying operational completion. Demand for that advantage remains unvalidated. [DataKart Trace](https://www.gs1india.org/datakart/datakart-trace)

## Constraints and implementation consequences

| Constraint | Consequence for the first version |
|---|---|
| Sources are sector-specific; public views may require JavaScript | Use a reviewed official notice or manufacturer disclosure as input; do not make a nationwide live-feed claim |
| Product names and ordinary barcodes do not always identify a batch | Match product/manufacturer/pack plus batch and any site/date restrictions; missing identifiers trigger evidence requests |
| No batch records means no reliable downstream batch tracing | Target a distributor already maintaining batches; do not infer missing history from total quantities |
| OCR can confuse identifiers and dates | Preserve originals and evidence locations; confirm ambiguous identifiers before mutating stock |
| Packs, cartons, loose units and returns can use different quantities | Store explicit unit conversions and reconcile stock, dispatch and return events |
| Sales may continue while a recall is processed | Use scoped mutations, stable action IDs and rereads; reconcile timeouts before retrying |
| Portal writes, accounting changes and external messages require permitted access | Initial version uses exported records and a sandbox inventory service; keep government reporting and communications reviewable |
| Digital containment differs from physical quarantine/return/disposal | Keep separate completion states and require receipts, inspections or acknowledgements for real-world steps |
| Incorrect matching can miss affected stock or disrupt unaffected stock | Use independently reviewed exact-match cases and verify unaffected records and operation history |
| Missing from a source is not a safety determination | Describe scope-specific findings and unresolved evidence; never issue a general safety certificate |
| Multiple languages increase extraction and translation complexity | Begin with English and one partner-relevant language, preserving identifiers and source meaning |
| Real business impact needs real records and operational validation | Label fixture records, failure injections and historical replay clearly; do not claim production savings from fixture runs |

## Sector boundaries

Food is the recommended first scope. CDSCO provides drug-quality and recall information, BIS publishes product recall alerts, and SIAM provides vehicle recall data, but their identifiers, action policies and completion requirements differ. Do not implement all four in the hackathon.

If pharmaceuticals are considered later, distinguish an NSQ quality-testing alert from an actual recall direction, a spurious-product alert and a blanket ban. A pharmacist-led action policy would be required. [CDSCO public NSQ view](https://cdscoonline.gov.in/CDSCO/viewPublicNSQDrug)

## Proposed completion contract

The first version can complete **digital recall reconciliation and containment** when every input record has a cited disposition, affected stock is confirmed held in the controlled system, shipment exposure is listed, quantities reconcile, and unresolved evidence and actions are visible. It must not label the entire physical or regulatory recall complete.

Suggested bounded build: one historical food recall, two warehouses, a handful of retailer accounts, batch stock and dispatch CSVs, invoice PDFs, a controlled hold tool, persistent case state and an independent verifier. The verifier checks rule boundaries, quantity conservation, unaffected stock, repeated operations and recovery after interruption.

Before implementation, establish a reviewed source scope and a representative inventory/dispatch schema. Source access, live ERP changes, automatic government submission and real message delivery remain unverified integrations.

"""One-shot localhost receiver: POST /<name> writes body to the raw alerts folder."""
import re
import sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(sys.argv[1])
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        name = self.path.strip("/")
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.json", name):
            self.send_response(400); self.end_headers(); return
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
        (OUT / name).write_bytes(body)
        print("saved", name, len(body), flush=True)
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"); self.end_headers()

    def do_OPTIONS(self):
        self.send_response(204)
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "*")
        self.end_headers()

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass


HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8765), H).serve_forever()

"""Parse NSQ rows copied from the CDSCO online portal (cdscoonline.gov.in/CDSCO/viewPublicNSQDrug).

Newer alerts are not PDFs: the portal renders one table per reporting month from JSON, with
month names ("Jun-2026") instead of MM/YYYY. data/alerts/raw/portal-<MON>-<YYYY>.jsonl holds each
row exactly as the portal served it, one JSON array per line, in this column order (the portal's
own field names, keys dropped to keep the files small):

    str_product_name, str_batch_no, dt_manufacturing_date, dt_expiry_date, str_manufactured_by,
    str_nsq_result, str_reporting_source, str_reported_by_lab_or_state, dt_reporting_month_year

Values are verbatim, including the portal's typos, stray line breaks and "?" placeholders.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path

from .alerts import AlertEntry, clean

COLUMNS = (
    "str_product_name",
    "str_batch_no",
    "dt_manufacturing_date",
    "dt_expiry_date",
    "str_manufactured_by",
    "str_nsq_result",
    "str_reporting_source",
    "str_reported_by_lab_or_state",
    "dt_reporting_month_year",
)
MONTHS = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(
    ("jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun", "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"), start=1)}
MON_YEAR_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z]{3})-(\d{4})\s*$")
NO_BATCH = {"", "not mentioned", "na", "n/a", "nil", "-"}


def parse_mon_year(cell: str | None) -> str | None:
    """"Jun-2026" / "AUG-2026" -> "2026-06" / "2026-08"; anything else -> None."""
    m = MON_YEAR_RE.match(cell or "")
    if not m or m.group(1).lower() not in MONTHS:
        return None
    return f"{int(m.group(2)):04d}-{MONTHS[m.group(1).lower()]:02d}"


def parse_portal_jsonl(path: str | Path) -> list[AlertEntry]:
    path = Path(path)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    entries: list[AlertEntry] = []
    for line_no, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        row = json.loads(line)
        if len(row) != len(COLUMNS):
            raise ValueError(f"{path.name}:{line_no}: expected {len(COLUMNS)} columns, got {len(row)}")
        raw = dict(zip(COLUMNS, row))
        batch = clean(raw["str_batch_no"])
        mfg, exp = parse_mon_year(raw["dt_manufacturing_date"]), parse_mon_year(raw["dt_expiry_date"])
        issues: list[str] = []
        if batch.lower() in NO_BATCH:
            issues.append(f"no usable batch number: {raw['str_batch_no']!r}")
        if raw["dt_manufacturing_date"] is None:
            issues.append("manufacturing date missing")
        elif mfg is None:
            issues.append(f"manufacturing date not Mon-YYYY: {raw['dt_manufacturing_date']!r}")
        if raw["dt_expiry_date"] is None:
            issues.append("expiry date missing")
        elif exp is None:
            issues.append(f"expiry date not Mon-YYYY: {raw['dt_expiry_date']!r}")
        if mfg and exp and exp < mfg:
            issues.append(f"expiry {exp} is before manufacture {mfg}")
        if batch != batch.strip(" ,"):
            issues.append("batch has stray punctuation")
        if re.search(r"[\r\n]", raw["str_batch_no"] or ""):
            issues.append("batch number was split across lines")
        entries.append(
            AlertEntry(
                source_file=path.name,
                source_sha256=digest,
                page=0,
                sno=str(line_no),
                product_name=clean(raw["str_product_name"]),
                batch_no=batch,
                mfg_month=mfg,
                expiry_month=exp,
                manufacturer=clean(raw["str_manufactured_by"]),
                nsq_result=clean(raw["str_nsq_result"]),
                lab=clean(raw["str_reported_by_lab_or_state"]),
                raw={k: raw[k] for k in ("str_batch_no", "dt_manufacturing_date", "dt_expiry_date")},
                issues=issues,
                reporting_source=clean(raw["str_reporting_source"]),
                report_month=parse_mon_year(raw["dt_reporting_month_year"]),
            )
        )
    return entries


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 2:
        print("usage: python -m recallops.portal <portal-MON-YYYY.jsonl> [out.json]")
        return 2
    src = Path(argv[1])
    entries = parse_portal_jsonl(src)
    out = Path(argv[2]) if len(argv) > 2 else Path("data/alerts/parsed") / (src.stem + ".json")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps([asdict(e) for e in entries], indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    bad = [e for e in entries if e.issues]
    print(f"{src.name}: {len(entries)} entries, {len(bad)} with parse issues -> {out}")
    for e in bad[:15]:
        print(f"  #{e.sno} {e.product_name[:40]!r} [{e.batch_no}]: {'; '.join(e.issues)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

"""Generate SYNTHETIC distributor records from real CDSCO NSQ alert batches.

Everything in data/fixtures is made up: the distributor, customers, quantities, invoices, dates and
every deliberate error. What is real is the set of alert rows (data/alerts/raw/portal-*.jsonl) that
the affected stock lots are built from, plus the real manufacturer and product names in them.
Every CSV carries a `_synthetic` column set to "Y" and the folder carries SYNTHETIC-FIXTURE.txt.

Two alert rounds are modelled, using the real portal months:
  round 1 = JUL-2026 alert,  round 2 = JUL-2026 + AUG-2026 (the second alert adds batches).

truth.json says, for every stock row and each round, what a careful operator should do:
  hold       strong evidence: batch (after trivial normalisation) + product + manufacturer or dates
  review     weak or conflicting evidence: must be escalated, never silently held or cleared
  no_hold    not an affected batch (decoys: sibling batches, batch-number collisions, unrelated)
A failure belongs to the tested batch only, so a "no_hold" is a scoped finding, not a safety clearance.

Usage: python -m recallops.fixtures [--seed N] [--out data/fixtures]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import random
import re
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from .alerts import AlertEntry
from .portal import parse_portal_jsonl

DEFAULT_SEED = 20261011
AS_OF = date(2026, 10, 10)
RAW = Path("data/alerts/raw")
MONTH_ABBR = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]

NON_DRUG = re.compile(
    r"soap|shampoo|bandage|cotton|gauze|guaze|syringe|chlorine|hajmola|wash|cleansing|formaldehyde|"
    r"cypermeth|diabetis|dr\.? puri|beauty|powder|drops|mouthwash|ors\b|oral rehydration", re.I)
SALT_WORDS = {
    "potassium", "sodium", "hydrochloride", "hcl", "hci", "sulphate", "sulfate", "maleate", "phosphate",
    "magnesium", "acetate", "dihydrochloride", "besilate", "tromethamine", "calcium", "hydrobromide", "citrate",
    "anhydrous", "gastro-resistant", "gastro", "resistant", "extended", "release", "prolonged", "sustained",
    "dispersible", "enteric", "coated", "controlled", "oral", "orally", "disintegrating"}
FORM_WORDS = {"tablets": "TAB", "tablet": "TAB", "capsules": "CAP", "capsule": "CAP", "injection": "INJ",
              "syrup": "SYP", "suspension": "SUSP", "ointment": "OINT", "cream": "CRM", "gel": "GEL"}
CITIES = [("Delhi", "DL"), ("Mumbai", "MH"), ("Pune", "MH"), ("Jaipur", "RJ"), ("Lucknow", "UP"),
          ("Chennai", "TN"), ("Bengaluru", "KA"), ("Hyderabad", "TS"), ("Kolkata", "WB"), ("Ahmedabad", "GJ"),
          ("Chandigarh", "CH"), ("Indore", "MP"), ("Kochi", "KL"), ("Patna", "BR"), ("Bhopal", "MP")]
CUSTOMER_STEMS = ["Green Cross Chemist", "City Medicals", "Sunrise Pharmacy", "Lifeline Drug House", "Apex Hospital Pharmacy",
                  "Care Plus Clinic", "Metro Health Stores", "Hope Nursing Home", "Royal Medicos", "Unity Pharmacy",
                  "Health First Chemist", "Pioneer Medical Hall", "Trust Hospital Stores", "Kalyan Medicals", "Nova Clinic Pharmacy",
                  "Shree Drug Agency", "Ocean View Pharmacy", "Silver Oak Medicos", "Midtown Chemists", "Evergreen Hospital Stores",
                  "Harmony Pharmacy", "Orbit Medical Stores", "Blue Cross Dispensary", "Lotus Chemists", "Vista Health Mart",
                  "Sai Medical Hall", "Zenith Pharma Retail", "Crest Clinic Dispensary"]


# ---------- text mess ----------

def norm_batch(b: str) -> str:
    """The trivial normalisation a matcher is allowed: case, separators, O/0 confusion."""
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", (b or "").upper()).replace("O", "0")


def short_mfr(manufacturer: str) -> str:
    head = re.split(r"[,.(\-]| {2,}| - |\n", manufacturer)[0]
    words = [w for w in head.split() if w.lower().strip(".") not in {"pvt", "ltd", "limited", "private", "llp", "p"}]
    return " ".join(words[:3]).title() or manufacturer[:20].title()


def abbreviate(product: str) -> str:
    """Pharmacy-counter shorthand: 'Amoxycillin & Potassium Clavulanate Tablets IP 625' -> 'Amox+Clav 625 TAB'."""
    text = re.sub(r"\(.*?\)", " ", product)
    form = next((FORM_WORDS[w] for w in re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text.lower()) if w in FORM_WORDS), "")
    strengths = re.findall(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s?(?:mg|mcg|ml|g|iu|%)", text, flags=re.I)
    base = re.split(r"\b(?:tablets?|capsules?|injection|syrup|suspension|ointment|cream|gel)\b", text, 1, flags=re.I)[0]
    parts = [p for p in re.split(r"\s*(?:,|&|\band\b|\bwith\b)\s*", base) if p.strip()]
    heads = []
    for p in parts:
        words = [w for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+", p) if w.lower() not in SALT_WORDS]
        if words:
            heads.append(words[0][:4].capitalize())
    name = "+".join(heads[:3]) or product[:8]
    if strengths:
        name += " " + re.sub(r"\s", "", strengths[0]).lower()
    return f"{name} {form}".strip()


def typo(name: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    words = name.split(" ")
    i = max(range(len(words)), key=lambda k: len(words[k]))
    w = words[i]
    if len(w) < 5:
        return name
    j = rng.randrange(1, len(w) - 2)
    words[i] = w[:j] + w[j + 1] + w[j] + w[j + 2:]
    return " ".join(words)


def batch_variant(b: str, rng: random.Random) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """A messy but same-batch spelling. Returns (text, how)."""
    clean_b = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", b).strip()
    options = ["lower", "nosep", "space", "comma", "pad"]
    if "0" in clean_b or "O" in clean_b.upper():
        options.append("o0")
    how = rng.choice(options)
    if how == "lower":
        return clean_b.lower(), how
    if how == "nosep":
        out = re.sub(r"[-/ .]", "", clean_b)
        return (out if out != clean_b else clean_b.lower()), (how if out != clean_b else "lower")
    if how == "space":
        k = max(2, len(clean_b) // 2)
        return clean_b[:k] + " " + clean_b[k:], how
    if how == "comma":
        return clean_b + ",", how
    if how == "pad":
        return f" {clean_b}  ", how
    idx = [i for i, c in enumerate(clean_b) if c in "0Oo"]
    i = rng.choice(idx)
    return clean_b[:i] + ("O" if clean_b[i] == "0" else "0") + clean_b[i + 1:], how


def sibling_batch(b: str, taken: set[str], rng: random.Random) -> str:
    """A different batch of the same product: change the last alphanumeric character."""
    chars = list(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", b).strip())
    for _ in range(50):
        c = list(chars)
        idx = [i for i, ch in enumerate(c) if ch.isalnum()]
        i = idx[-1] if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.choice(idx)
        if c[i].isdigit():
            c[i] = str((int(c[i]) + rng.randint(1, 8)) % 10)
        else:
            c[i] = chr(ord("A") + (ord(c[i].upper()) - ord("A") + rng.randint(1, 20)) % 26)
        cand = "".join(c)
        if norm_batch(cand) not in taken:
            return cand
    return b + "9"


def fake_batch(rng: random.Random, taken: set[str]) -> str:
    while True:
        pat = rng.choice(["{L}{L}{D}{D}{D}{D}", "{D}{D}{D}{D}{D}{D}", "{L}{D}{D}{D}{D}{L}", "{L}{L}-{D}{D}{D}", "T{D}{D}{D}{D}{D}"])
        out = pat.replace("{L}", "@").replace("{D}", "#")
        b = "".join(rng.choice("ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTVWXYZ") if ch == "@" else str(rng.randint(0, 9)) if ch == "#" else ch for ch in out)
        if norm_batch(b) not in taken:
            return b


def month_text(ym: str | None, rng: random.Random, style: str) -> str:
    if not ym:
        return ""
    y, m = int(ym[:4]), int(ym[5:])
    if style == "mm/yyyy":
        return f"{m:02d}/{y}"
    if style == "mon-yy":
        return f"{MONTH_ABBR[m - 1]}-{y % 100:02d}"
    if style == "yyyy-mm":
        return f"{y}-{m:02d}"
    if style == "dd/mm/yyyy":
        return f"{rng.choice([1, 28]):02d}/{m:02d}/{y}"
    return f"{MONTH_ABBR[m - 1]} {y}"


def shift_month(ym: str, delta: int) -> str:
    y, m = int(ym[:4]), int(ym[5:])
    k = y * 12 + (m - 1) + delta
    return f"{k // 12:04d}-{k % 12 + 1:02d}"


# ---------- generator ----------

def build(seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED, out: str | Path = "data/fixtures", raw_dir: Path = RAW) -> dict:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    jul = parse_portal_jsonl(raw_dir / "portal-JUL-2026.jsonl")
    aug = parse_portal_jsonl(raw_dir / "portal-AUG-2026.jsonl")
    all_alert = jul + aug
    alert_batches = {norm_batch(e.batch_no) for e in all_alert}

    def usable(e: AlertEntry) -> bool:
        return not e.issues and not NON_DRUG.search(e.product_name)

    # Group alert rows that are the same physical batch (real data reports some batches twice).
    def group(entries: list[AlertEntry]) -> dict[str, list[AlertEntry]]:
        g: dict[str, list[AlertEntry]] = {}
        for e in entries:
            if e.batch_no and "Not Mentioned" not in e.batch_no:
                key = norm_batch(e.batch_no) + "|" + short_mfr(e.manufacturer).lower()[:8]
                g.setdefault(key, []).append(e)
        return g

    jul_groups, aug_groups = group([e for e in jul if usable(e) or e.batch_no in ("T-2611 36",)]), group([e for e in aug if usable(e)])
    forced_jul = [k for k in jul_groups if k.startswith(("25460922|", "I7881|", "MWDC5421G|", "18260226A|", "25CT0314|"))]
    forced_aug = [k for k in aug_groups if k.startswith(("25460922|", "BKBP02601|"))]
    jul_pick = forced_jul + rng.sample([k for k in jul_groups if k not in forced_jul], 58 - len(forced_jul) + 0)
    aug_pick = forced_aug + rng.sample([k for k in aug_groups if k not in forced_aug and k not in jul_pick], 30 - len(forced_aug))

    items: list[dict] = []
    stock: list[dict] = []
    lots: dict[str, dict] = {}
    mfr_pool = sorted({short_mfr(e.manufacturer) for e in all_alert})
    taken = set(alert_batches)

    def new_item(name: str, mfr: str) -> str:
        code = f"IT{len(items) + 1:04d}"
        items.append({"item_code": code, "item_name": name, "mfr_name": mfr,
                      "units_per_box": rng.choice([10, 10, 6, 12, 15]), "_synthetic": "Y"})
        return code

    def add_lot(item_code: str, role: str, batch_raw: str, mfg: str | None, exp: str | None, refs: dict,
                expected: dict, mess: list[str], warehouse: str | None = None, extra: dict | None = None) -> str:
        lot_id = f"L{len(lots) + 1:04d}"
        warehouse = warehouse or rng.choice(["WH-DEL", "WH-MUM"])
        lots[lot_id] = {"lot_id": lot_id, "item_code": item_code, "role": role, "batch_true_text": batch_raw,
                        "alert_refs": refs, "expected": expected, "mess": mess, "stock_ids": [],
                        "mfg_month": mfg, "expiry_month": exp, "warehouse": warehouse, **(extra or {})}
        return lot_id

    # --- affected lots from real alert rows
    def make_affected(rows: list[AlertEntry], origin: str, profile: str) -> None:
        e = rows[0]
        refs: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for r in rows:
            refs.setdefault(r.report_month or "?", []).append(r.sno)
        mess: list[str] = []
        name = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", e.product_name).strip().rstrip(",.)")
        mfr = short_mfr(e.manufacturer)
        batch = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", e.batch_no).strip().rstrip(",")
        mfg_s, exp_s = e.mfg_month, e.expiry_month
        action = "hold"
        if profile == "exact":
            pass
        elif profile == "norm_batch":
            batch, how = batch_variant(batch, rng)
            mess.append(f"batch:{how}")
        elif profile == "abbrev_name":
            name = abbreviate(name)
            mess.append("name:abbrev")
        elif profile == "typo_name":
            name = typo(name, rng)
            mess.append("name:typo")
        elif profile == "no_dates":
            mfg_s = exp_s = None
            mess.append("dates:blank")
        elif profile == "no_mfr":
            mfr = ""
            mess.append("mfr:blank")
        elif profile == "weak":
            name = abbreviate(name)
            batch, how = batch_variant(batch, rng)
            mfr, mfg_s, exp_s = "", None, None
            mess += ["name:abbrev", f"batch:{how}", "mfr:blank", "dates:blank"]
            action = "review"
        code = new_item(name, mfr)
        in_jul = any(r.report_month == "2026-07" for r in rows)
        expected = {"1": action if in_jul else "no_hold", "2": action}
        lot_id = add_lot(code, "affected", batch, mfg_s, exp_s, refs, expected, mess,
                         extra={"origin": origin, "alert_batch": e.batch_no, "evidence": "weak" if action == "review" else "strong",
                                "reopened_in_round_2": not in_jul})
        # lots with strong evidence sometimes sit in both warehouses
        if action == "hold" and rng.random() < 0.25:
            lots[lot_id]["split_warehouse"] = True

    profiles = ["exact"] * 34 + ["norm_batch"] * 22 + ["abbrev_name"] * 14 + ["typo_name"] * 6 + ["no_dates"] * 6 + ["no_mfr"] * 6 + ["weak"] * 6
    rng.shuffle(profiles)
    pi = iter(profiles * 3)
    for key in jul_pick:
        make_affected(jul_groups[key], "JUL-2026", next(pi))
    for key in aug_pick:
        make_affected(aug_groups[key], "AUG-2026", "weak" if len([l for l in lots.values() if l["evidence"] == "weak"]) < 3 and rng.random() < 0.1 else next(pi))
    n_affected = len(lots)
    affected_by_item = {l["item_code"]: l for l in lots.values()}

    # --- siblings: same item, different batch, different dates (name-only matching holds these wrongly)
    for lot in list(lots.values()):
        if lot["role"] != "affected" or rng.random() > 0.65:
            continue
        for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2])):
            near = rng.random() < 0.5
            b = sibling_batch(lot["batch_true_text"], taken, rng)
            taken.add(norm_batch(b))
            base = lot["mfg_month"] or "2025-06"
            add_lot(lot["item_code"], "sibling_near" if near else "sibling", b, shift_month(base, rng.choice([-5, -3, 3, 5])),
                    shift_month(base, rng.choice([19, 21, 29, 31])), {}, {"1": "no_hold", "2": "no_hold"},
                    ["different batch of an affected product"], extra={"sibling_of": lot["lot_id"]})

    # --- manufacturer mismatch: product + batch match an alert row but the manufacturer is another company
    jul_lots = [l for l in lots.values() if l["role"] == "affected" and l["origin"] == "JUL-2026" and l["evidence"] == "strong"]
    for src in rng.sample(jul_lots, 6):
        src_item = next(i for i in items if i["item_code"] == src["item_code"])
        other = rng.choice([m for m in mfr_pool if m.lower()[:8] != src_item["mfr_name"].lower()[:8]])
        code = new_item(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", src_item["item_name"]), other)
        add_lot(code, "mfr_mismatch", src["batch_true_text"], src["mfg_month"], src["expiry_month"], {}, {"1": "review", "2": "review"},
                ["same batch and product text as an alert row but a different manufacturer"], extra={"mirrors": src["lot_id"]})

    # --- unrelated products from the other (unselected) alert rows, fabricated batches
    picked_batches = {norm_batch(l["alert_batch"]) for l in lots.values() if l["role"] == "affected"}
    other_rows = [e for e in all_alert if usable(e) and norm_batch(e.batch_no) not in picked_batches]
    rng.shuffle(other_rows)
    unrelated_items: list[tuple[str, AlertEntry]] = []
    for e in other_rows[:70]:
        code = new_item(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", e.product_name).strip().rstrip(",.)"), short_mfr(e.manufacturer))
        unrelated_items.append((code, e))
        for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2])):
            b = fake_batch(rng, taken)
            taken.add(norm_batch(b))
            mfg = shift_month("2025-01", rng.randint(0, 14))
            add_lot(code, "unrelated", b, mfg, shift_month(mfg, 24), {}, {"1": "no_hold", "2": "no_hold"}, [])

    # --- batch-number collisions: a different product whose batch equals an alert batch
    short_alerts = [e for e in all_alert if usable(e) and len(norm_batch(e.batch_no)) <= 5][:40]
    for e in rng.sample(short_alerts, min(8, len(short_alerts))):
        code, src = rng.choice(unrelated_items)
        if norm_batch(src.batch_no) == norm_batch(e.batch_no) or src.product_name == e.product_name:
            continue
        add_lot(code, "collision", e.batch_no, "2025-03", "2027-02", {}, {"1": "no_hold", "2": "no_hold"},
                ["batch number equals an alert batch of a different product"], extra={"collides_with": e.batch_no})

    # ---------- stock rows, purchases, customers, sales ----------
    date_styles = ["mm/yyyy", "mon-yy", "yyyy-mm", "dd/mm/yyyy", "mon yyyy"]
    purchases: list[dict] = []
    sales: list[dict] = []
    item_by_code = {i["item_code"]: i for i in items}
    customers = []
    for n, stem in enumerate(CUSTOMER_STEMS, start=1):
        city, st = rng.choice(CITIES)
        customers.append({"customer_id": f"C{n:03d}", "name": f"[SYNTHETIC] {stem}",
                          "type": "hospital" if "Hospital" in stem or "Nursing" in stem else "clinic" if "Clinic" in stem else "pharmacy",
                          "city": city, "state": st, "contact_email": f"c{n:03d}@example.invalid", "_synthetic": "Y"})
    suppliers = ["SYNTH TRADERS NORTH", "SYNTH TRADERS WEST", "SYNTH TRADERS SOUTH"]
    inv_no = 0
    line_no = 0
    ledger_gap_lots = set(rng.sample([k for k, l in lots.items() if l["role"] in ("affected", "unrelated")], 5))

    for lot_id, lot in lots.items():
        item = item_by_code[lot["item_code"]]
        upb = item["units_per_box"]
        boxes = rng.randint(4, 40)
        received = boxes * upb
        mfg_m = lot["mfg_month"]
        p_month = shift_month(mfg_m, rng.randint(1, 4)) if mfg_m else "2025-09"
        p_date = date(int(p_month[:4]), int(p_month[5:]), rng.randint(1, 27))
        if p_date > AS_OF - timedelta(days=30):
            p_date = AS_OF - timedelta(days=rng.randint(40, 120))
        inv_no += 1
        mfr_name = item["mfr_name"]
        purchases.append({"purchase_invoice": f"PI-{inv_no:05d}", "date": p_date.isoformat(),
                          "supplier": rng.choice([mfr_name or suppliers[0], mfr_name or suppliers[1], rng.choice(suppliers)]),
                          "item_code": item["item_code"], "batch_raw": lot["batch_true_text"], "qty_boxes": boxes,
                          "units_per_box": upb, "warehouse": lot["warehouse"], "_synthetic": "Y"})
        sold_total = int(received * rng.choice([0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9])) if lot["role"] != "mfr_mismatch" else int(received * 0.3)
        n_lines = 0 if sold_total == 0 else rng.randint(1, 4)
        left = sold_total
        for k in range(n_lines):
            qty = left if k == n_lines - 1 else max(1, int(left * rng.uniform(0.2, 0.6)))
            left -= qty
            if qty <= 0:
                continue
            line_no += 1
            c = rng.choice(customers)
            s_date = p_date + timedelta(days=rng.randint(5, 150))
            s_date = min(s_date, AS_OF - timedelta(days=rng.randint(1, 20)))
            blank = lot["role"] == "affected" and rng.random() < 0.12
            b_text = "" if blank else (batch_variant(lot["batch_true_text"], rng)[0] if rng.random() < 0.2 else lot["batch_true_text"])
            sales.append({"sale_line": f"SL-{line_no:05d}", "invoice_no": f"SI-{(line_no + 1) // 2 + 1000:05d}", "date": s_date.isoformat(),
                          "customer_id": c["customer_id"], "item_code": item["item_code"], "batch_raw": b_text,
                          "qty_units": qty, "warehouse": lot["warehouse"], "_synthetic": "Y", "_lot": lot_id})
        on_hand = received - sold_total
        gap = 0
        if lot_id in ledger_gap_lots and on_hand > 30:
            gap = rng.randint(5, 20)
            lot["ledger_gap_units"] = gap
        lot["received_units"], lot["sold_units"], lot["on_hand_true_units"] = received, sold_total, on_hand
        # one stock row, or two when the lot is split across warehouses
        splits = [(lot["warehouse"], on_hand + gap)]
        if lot.get("split_warehouse") and on_hand >= 20:
            first = on_hand // 2
            other = "WH-MUM" if lot["warehouse"] == "WH-DEL" else "WH-DEL"
            splits = [(lot["warehouse"], first + gap), (other, on_hand - first)]
        style = rng.choice(date_styles)
        for wh, qty in splits:
            sid = f"S{len(stock) + 1:04d}"
            stock.append({"stock_id": sid, "warehouse": wh, "item_code": item["item_code"], "batch_raw": lot["batch_true_text"],
                          "mfg_raw": month_text(lot["mfg_month"], rng, style), "expiry_raw": month_text(lot["expiry_month"], rng, style),
                          "qty_units": qty, "status": "AVAILABLE", "_synthetic": "Y", "_lot": lot_id})
            lot["stock_ids"].append(sid)

    # ---------- truth ----------
    stock_truth = {}
    for row in stock:
        lot = lots[row["_lot"]]
        stock_truth[row["stock_id"]] = {"lot_id": lot["lot_id"], "role": lot["role"], "expected": lot["expected"], "mess": lot["mess"]}
    exposure: dict[str, dict] = {"1": {}, "2": {}}
    unresolved_lines: dict[str, list] = {"1": [], "2": []}
    hold_items = {r: {lots[l]["item_code"] for l in lots if lots[l]["expected"][r] == "hold"} for r in ("1", "2")}
    for s in sales:
        lot = lots[s["_lot"]]
        for r in ("1", "2"):
            if lot["expected"][r] == "hold" and s["batch_raw"]:
                exposure[r].setdefault(s["customer_id"], []).append(s["sale_line"])
            elif lot["expected"][r] == "hold" and not s["batch_raw"]:
                unresolved_lines[r].append(s["sale_line"])
    truth = {
        "synthetic": True, "seed": seed, "as_of": AS_OF.isoformat(),
        "rounds": {"1": {"alerts": ["portal-JUL-2026"]}, "2": {"alerts": ["portal-JUL-2026", "portal-AUG-2026"]}},
        "expected_actions": ["hold", "review", "no_hold"],
        "note": "no_hold is a scoped finding about listed batches, never a safety clearance.",
        "stock": stock_truth,
        "lots": {k: {kk: vv for kk, vv in v.items() if kk != "stock_ids"} | {"stock_ids": v["stock_ids"]} for k, v in lots.items()},
        "exposed_customers": {r: {c: sorted(v) for c, v in d.items()} for r, d in exposure.items()},
        "unresolved_sales_lines": {r: sorted(v) for r, v in unresolved_lines.items()},
    }

    out = Path(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    write_csv(out / "items.csv", items)
    write_csv(out / "stock.csv", [{k: v for k, v in r.items() if not k.startswith("_lot")} for r in stock])
    write_csv(out / "purchases.csv", purchases)
    write_csv(out / "customers.csv", customers)
    write_csv(out / "sales.csv", [{k: v for k, v in r.items() if k != "_lot"} for r in sales])
    (out / "truth.json").write_text(json.dumps(truth, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "SYNTHETIC-FIXTURE.txt").write_text(
        "SYNTHETIC DATA. The distributor, customers, quantities, invoices and dates in this folder are invented.\n"
        "Only the alert rows they are built from (data/alerts/raw) are real CDSCO NSQ data.\n"
        "truth.json (the answer key) is for evaluation only and must not be given to the agent.\n", encoding="utf-8")
    counts = {}
    for l in lots.values():
        counts[l["role"]] = counts.get(l["role"], 0) + 1
    return {"lots": len(lots), "stock_rows": len(stock), "items": len(items), "sales_lines": len(sales),
            "purchases": len(purchases), "roles": counts,
            "expected_round1": count_actions(stock_truth, "1"), "expected_round2": count_actions(stock_truth, "2")}


def count_actions(stock_truth: dict, rnd: str) -> dict:
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    for t in stock_truth.values():
        out[t["expected"][rnd]] = out.get(t["expected"][rnd], 0) + 1
    return out


def write_csv(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=DEFAULT_SEED)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/fixtures")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(build(args.seed, args.out), indent=1))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Score a run against the fixture answer key (data/fixtures/truth.json).

Observed outcome per stock row is read from the stock service itself, not from what the run claims:
  HELD in the service            -> "hold"
  still AVAILABLE and flagged    -> "review"
  still AVAILABLE, not flagged   -> "no_hold"
Expected outcome comes from truth.json for the alert round being scored.

Metrics (counts of stock rows):
  correct_hold    expected hold,   observed hold
  missed_hold     expected hold,   observed no_hold          <- safety failure
  wrong_hold      expected no_hold, observed hold            <- cost failure (good stock frozen)
  review_ok       expected review, observed review
  review_held     expected review, observed hold             <- acted without escalating
  review_cleared  expected review, observed no_hold          <- silently cleared an uncertain row
  needless_review expected hold/no_hold, observed review     <- workload, not an error of safety
Also: customers_recall (exposed customers found / total) when a trace is provided.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from .stockservice import StockService

TRUTH = Path("data/fixtures/truth.json")


def load_truth(path: str | Path = TRUTH) -> dict:
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def observed(service: StockService, flagged_for_review: set[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    out = {}
    for row in service.list_stock():
        sid = row["stock_id"]
        out[sid] = "hold" if row["status"] == "HELD" else "review" if sid in flagged_for_review else "no_hold"
    return out


def score(service: StockService, flagged_for_review: set[str], truth: dict, rnd: str,
          traced_customers: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None) -> dict:
    obs = observed(service, flagged_for_review)
    m = {k: 0 for k in ("correct_hold", "missed_hold", "wrong_hold", "review_ok", "review_held", "review_cleared", "needless_review")}
    wrong, missed = [], []
    for sid, t in truth["stock"].items():
        exp, got = t["expected"][rnd], obs[sid]
        if exp == "hold" and got == "hold":
            m["correct_hold"] += 1
        elif exp == "hold" and got == "no_hold":
            m["missed_hold"] += 1
            missed.append(sid)
        elif exp == "no_hold" and got == "hold":
            m["wrong_hold"] += 1
            wrong.append(sid)
        elif exp == "review" and got == "review":
            m["review_ok"] += 1
        elif exp == "review" and got == "hold":
            m["review_held"] += 1
        elif exp == "review" and got == "no_hold":
            m["review_cleared"] += 1
        elif got == "review":
            m["needless_review"] += 1
    expected_holds = sum(1 for t in truth["stock"].values() if t["expected"][rnd] == "hold")
    m["expected_holds"] = expected_holds
    m["total_rows"] = len(truth["stock"])
    m["wrong_hold_ids"], m["missed_hold_ids"] = wrong, missed
    if traced_customers is not None:
        exposed = set(truth["exposed_customers"][rnd])
        found = set(traced_customers)
        m["customers_exposed"] = len(exposed)
        m["customers_found"] = len(exposed & found)
        m["customers_extra"] = len(found - exposed)
    return m


def summary_line(m: dict) -> str:
    return (f"correct {m['correct_hold']}/{m['expected_holds']}  missed {m['missed_hold']}  wrong {m['wrong_hold']}  "
            f"review ok {m['review_ok']} held-unreviewed {m['review_held']} cleared {m['review_cleared']} needless {m['needless_review']}")

"""The "before": naive name-only matching.

For every stock row, normalise the item name and the alert product name (lower-case, drop dosage-form
and pharmacopoeia words, drop strengths, sort the remaining words) and hold the row if the two agree,
or are very close. It ignores batch, manufacturer and dates, which is what a rushed operator or a
simple script does, and it never asks for a review. No model calls.

Expected failure modes (they are the point): it holds every sibling batch of an affected product, and
it misses stock whose item name is shorthand ("Amox+Clav 625 TAB").
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from pathlib import Path

from .alerts import AlertEntry
from .evaluate import load_truth, score, summary_line
from .portal import parse_portal_jsonl
from .stockservice import StockService

RAW = Path("data/alerts/raw")
STOP = {"tablets", "tablet", "capsules", "capsule", "injection", "syrup", "suspension", "oral", "ip", "i", "p", "usp", "bp",
        "mg", "mcg", "ml", "g", "iu", "w", "v", "for", "and", "with", "of", "the", "gastro", "resistant", "tab", "cap", "inj", "syp", "susp"}
FUZZY = 0.9


def name_key(name: str) -> str:
    text = re.sub(r"\(.*?\)", " ", name.lower())
    words = [w for w in re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text) if w not in STOP and len(w) > 1]
    return " ".join(sorted(words))


def alerts_for_round(rnd: str, raw_dir: Path = RAW) -> list[AlertEntry]:
    months = ["JUL"] if rnd == "1" else ["JUL", "AUG"]
    out: list[AlertEntry] = []
    for m in months:
        out += parse_portal_jsonl(raw_dir / f"portal-{m}-2026.jsonl")
    return out


def run_baseline(service: StockService, alerts: list[AlertEntry]) -> dict:
    items = service.items()
    alert_keys = {name_key(a.product_name) for a in alerts if a.product_name}
    alert_keys.discard("")
    held = []
    for row in service.list_stock("AVAILABLE"):
        key = name_key(items[row["item_code"]]["item_name"])
        if key and (key in alert_keys or any(SequenceMatcher(None, key, k).ratio() >= FUZZY for k in alert_keys)):
            service.place_hold(row["stock_id"], "name-only match to NSQ alert", action_id=f"baseline-{row['stock_id']}")
            held.append(row["stock_id"])
    return {"held": held}


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--round", choices=["1", "2"], default="1")
    ap.add_argument("--fixtures", default="data/fixtures")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    service = StockService(fixtures_dir=args.fixtures)
    result = run_baseline(service, alerts_for_round(args.round))
    m = score(service, set(), load_truth(Path(args.fixtures) / "truth.json"), args.round)
    print(f"baseline round {args.round}: held {len(result['held'])} rows | {summary_line(m)}")
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in m.items() if not k.endswith("_ids")}))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Stock service state transitions, the scorer, and the name-only baseline, on the synthetic fixtures."""
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from recallops.baseline import alerts_for_round, name_key, run_baseline
from recallops.evaluate import load_truth, score
from recallops.stockservice import StockError, StockService

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
FIX = ROOT / "data" / "fixtures"
RAW = ROOT / "data" / "alerts" / "raw"


@pytest.fixture()
def svc():
    return StockService(fixtures_dir=FIX)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def truth():
    return load_truth(FIX / "truth.json")


def test_hold_is_a_real_state_change_and_replay_is_idempotent(svc):
    sid = svc.list_stock("AVAILABLE")[0]["stock_id"]
    first = svc.place_hold(sid, "test", action_id="a1")
    assert first == {"stock_id": sid, "status": "HELD", "replayed": False}
    assert svc.get_stock(sid)["status"] == "HELD"
    again = svc.place_hold(sid, "test", action_id="a1")  # same action id: no second write
    assert again["replayed"] is True
    assert len(svc.events()) == 1
    with pytest.raises(StockError):  # a fresh action id on a held row is a visible conflict
        svc.place_hold(sid, "test", action_id="a2")


def test_injected_timeout_leaves_a_durable_hold(svc):
    sid = svc.list_stock("AVAILABLE")[0]["stock_id"]
    svc.inject_timeout_after_write(1)
    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
        svc.place_hold(sid, "test", action_id="t1")
    assert svc.get_stock(sid)["status"] == "HELD"  # the write happened although the caller saw a failure
    assert svc.place_hold(sid, "test", action_id="t1")["replayed"] is True  # retry is safe
    assert len(svc.events()) == 1


def test_release_returns_row_to_available(svc):
    sid = svc.list_stock("AVAILABLE")[0]["stock_id"]
    svc.place_hold(sid, "x", action_id="h")
    svc.release_hold(sid, "x", action_id="r")
    assert svc.get_stock(sid)["status"] == "AVAILABLE"
    with pytest.raises(StockError):
        svc.release_hold(sid, "x", action_id="r2")


def test_name_key_ignores_form_strength_and_order():
    assert name_key("Paracetamol Tablets IP 650mg") == name_key("PARACETAMOL tablets I.P. 500 mg") == "paracetamol"
    assert name_key("Amoxycillin & Potassium Clavulanate Tablets IP") == name_key("Potassium Clavulanate and Amoxycillin Tablets")
    assert name_key("Amox+Clav 625 TAB") != name_key("Amoxycillin & Potassium Clavulanate Tablets IP")  # shorthand defeats it


def test_baseline_holds_siblings_and_misses_shorthand(svc, truth):
    run_baseline(svc, alerts_for_round("1", RAW))
    m = score(svc, set(), truth, "1")
    assert m["correct_hold"] > 0
    assert m["wrong_hold"] > 0, "a name-only matcher should freeze sibling batches"
    assert m["missed_hold"] > 0, "a name-only matcher should miss shorthand item names"
    assert m["review_ok"] == 0  # the baseline never escalates
    sibs = [s for s, t in truth["stock"].items() if t["role"] in ("sibling", "sibling_near")]
    assert any(svc.get_stock(s)["status"] == "HELD" for s in sibs)


def test_scoring_reads_service_state_not_claims(svc, truth):
    m0 = score(svc, set(), truth, "1")
    assert m0["correct_hold"] == 0 and m0["missed_hold"] == m0["expected_holds"]
    hold_sid = next(s for s, t in truth["stock"].items() if t["expected"]["1"] == "hold")
    svc.place_hold(hold_sid, "x", action_id="z")
    assert score(svc, set(), truth, "1")["correct_hold"] == 1
    review_sid = next(s for s, t in truth["stock"].items() if t["expected"]["1"] == "review")
    assert score(svc, {review_sid}, truth, "1")["review_ok"] == 1
EOF

"""Thin OpenAI-compatible client for the hackathon LiteLLM gateway, with a hard call cap.

Config comes from the environment (.env is loaded, never printed):
  LITELLM_API_KEY   gateway key
  LLM_BASE_URL      default https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1
  LLM_MODEL         default model for judgement calls (default nova-lite, the cheap one)
  LLM_DRAFT_MODEL   model for drafted notices (default claude-haiku)
  RECALLOPS_MAX_LLM_CALLS   refuse further calls after this many (default 150); the budget is $20 in total
The code does the matching and arithmetic; the model is only asked about ambiguous names/aliases and
to draft notices.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time

from . import tracing

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1"


class BudgetExceeded(Exception):
    pass


class LLM:
    def __init__(self, model: str | None = None, draft_model: str | None = None, max_calls: int | None = None):
        from dotenv import load_dotenv

        load_dotenv()
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL", "nova-lite")
        self.draft_model = draft_model or os.environ.get("LLM_DRAFT_MODEL", "claude-haiku")
        self.max_calls = max_calls if max_calls is not None else int(os.environ.get("RECALLOPS_MAX_LLM_CALLS", "150"))
        self.calls = 0
        self.prompt_tokens = 0
        self.completion_tokens = 0
        self._client = None

    @property
    def client(self):
        if self._client is None:
            import openai  # imported late: neatlogs.init() has to run first

            key = os.environ.get("LITELLM_API_KEY")
            if not key:
                raise RuntimeError("LITELLM_API_KEY is not set (put it in .env)")
            self._client = tracing.wrap_client(openai.OpenAI(api_key=key, base_url=os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", DEFAULT_BASE_URL), timeout=60))
        return self._client

    def complete(self, system: str, user: str, *, draft: bool = False, max_tokens: int = 300) -> str:
        if self.calls >= self.max_calls:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"LLM call cap of {self.max_calls} reached")
        self.calls += 1
        last = None
        for attempt in range(2):
            try:
                r = self.client.chat.completions.create(
                    model=self.draft_model if draft else self.model, temperature=0, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                    messages=[{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}])
                if r.usage:
                    self.prompt_tokens += r.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
                    self.completion_tokens += r.usage.completion_tokens or 0
                return (r.choices[0].message.content or "").strip()
            except Exception as e:  # network blips, gateway 5xx: one retry, then surface
                last = e
                time.sleep(1.5)
        raise last

    def usage(self) -> dict:
        return {"calls": self.calls, "prompt_tokens": self.prompt_tokens, "completion_tokens": self.completion_tokens}

"""Run the baseline or the agent over both alert rounds and score against the fixture answer key.

  python -m recallops.run baseline
  python -m recallops.run agent [--no-llm] [--inject-timeout N] [--name my-run]

The baseline is stateless (a fresh stock service per round). The agent keeps one case across rounds, so
round 2 reopens decisions from round 1. Output goes to runs/<name>/ (git-ignored).
Each process traces under one neatlogs workflow name: recallops-baseline or recallops-agent.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import tracing
from .agent import Agent
from .baseline import alerts_for_round, run_baseline
from .evaluate import load_truth, score, summary_line
from .stockservice import StockService

FIXTURES = Path("data/fixtures")


def _metrics_view(m: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: v for k, v in m.items() if not k.endswith("_ids")}


@tracing.span("WORKFLOW", "recallops_baseline_run", capture_input=False)
def baseline_workflow(rounds: list[str], out: Path) -> dict:
    truth, results = load_truth(FIXTURES / "truth.json"), {}
    for rnd in rounds:
        t0 = time.time()
        service = StockService(db_path=out / f"stock-round{rnd}.sqlite", fixtures_dir=FIXTURES)
        run_baseline(service, alerts_for_round(rnd))
        m = score(service, set(), truth, rnd)
        results[rnd] = {**_metrics_view(m), "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 2), "llm_calls": 0}
        print(f"baseline round {rnd}: {summary_line(m)}")
    return results


@tracing.span("WORKFLOW", "recallops_agent_run", capture_input=False)
def agent_workflow(rounds: list[str], out: Path, llm, inject_timeout: int, inject_round: str) -> dict:
    truth, results = load_truth(FIXTURES / "truth.json"), {}
    service = StockService(db_path=out / "stock.sqlite", fixtures_dir=FIXTURES)
    agent = Agent(service, llm, out)
    for rnd in rounds:
        t0 = time.time()
        if inject_timeout and rnd == inject_round:
            service.inject_timeout_after_write(inject_timeout)
        report = agent.process_alert(alerts_for_round(rnd), rnd)
        m = score(service, report["_review_ids"], truth, rnd, report["_traced_customers"])
        results[rnd] = {**_metrics_view(m), "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 2), "llm_calls": report["llm_calls_this_round"],
                        "reopened": len(report["reopened_decisions"]), "recovery_events": len(report["recovery_events"]),
                        "duplicate_hold_events": report["verification"]["duplicate_hold_events"],
                        "verification_problems": len(report["verification"]["problems"]), "unresolved_invoice_lines": report["downstream"]["unresolved_invoice_lines"]}
        print(f"agent round {rnd}: {summary_line(m)} | customers {m['customers_found']}/{m['customers_exposed']} (+{m['customers_extra']}) | "
              f"llm calls {report['llm_calls_this_round']} | reopened {len(report['reopened_decisions'])} | recoveries {len(report['recovery_events'])}")
    if llm:
        results["llm_usage"] = llm.usage()
    return results


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=["baseline", "agent"])
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", default="1,2")
    ap.add_argument("--name", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--no-llm", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--inject-timeout", type=int, default=0, help="make the next N place_hold calls time out after writing")
    ap.add_argument("--inject-round", default="2")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    name = args.name or f"{args.mode}-{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
    out = Path("runs") / name
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    traced = tracing.setup(f"recallops-{args.mode}", tags=["hackathon", "synthetic-fixtures"])
    rounds = args.rounds.split(",")
    t0 = time.time()
    if args.mode == "baseline":
        results = baseline_workflow(rounds, out)
    else:
        from .llm import LLM

        results = agent_workflow(rounds, out, None if args.no_llm else LLM(), args.inject_timeout, args.inject_round)
    results["_run"] = {"name": name, "mode": args.mode, "traced": traced, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 2),
                       "inject_timeout": args.inject_timeout}
    (out / "metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    tracing.flush()
    print(f"metrics -> {out / 'metrics.json'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
